findings.doc_quote: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, glob string, or callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/types/types.py:330 — "FalseySentinel | V | Condition[V | FalseySentinel] | ComparisonCondition[V | FalseySentinel] | None"; src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:763-765 — `if not callable(condition): ... return coerce_to_literal_type(actual, condition) == condition`
findings.explanation: ChangeType has no glob-string member. A string is an ordinary literal and compare_value tests it for equality. Runtime probe: compare_value('light.kitchen', 'light.*') returned False. Only ServiceDataWhere (with auto_glob) and the DomainMatches/EntityMatches/ServiceMatches predicates detect globs.
findings.suggested_fix: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, or callable (value) -> bool. A bare string is compared exactly; use C.Glob for pattern matching.

findings.explanation: The dataclass field is named fn, not predicate. Runtime probe: P.Guard(predicate=...) raised TypeError: Guard.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'predicate'. Positional calls work.

findings.doc_quote: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, a glob string, or any callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:321-322 — `extracted = self.source(value); return compare_value(extracted, self.condition)`; predicates.py:763-765 — non-callable conditions use `==` with no glob handling
findings.explanation: P.ValueIs never interprets a string as a glob. A condition like "light.*" only matches the exact string "light.*", so a user following this line silently gets no matches. StateFrom, StateTo, AttrFrom and AttrTo delegate to ValueIs and behave the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, or any callable (value) -> bool. Strings are compared exactly; wrap a pattern in C.Glob to match it as a glob.

findings.doc_quote: When old_state is None , returns False even if the attribute is present on the new state.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:530-531 — `if value.payload.data.old_state is None: return get_attr_new(self.attr_name)(value) is not MISSING_VALUE`
findings.explanation: The code does the opposite. With no old state, the predicate returns True when the attribute is present on the new state, and False only when it is absent.
findings.suggested_fix: When old_state is None, returns True if the attribute is present on the new state, and False otherwise.

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when the string value contains substring , ignoring case.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:227 — `return isinstance(value, str) and self.substring in value`
findings.explanation: The check is a plain case-sensitive `in`. Runtime probe: C.Contains('KITCHEN')('light.kitchen') returned False.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when the string value contains substring (case-sensitive).

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:120-122 — `if isinstance(collection, str): raise ValueError("collection must be a sequence of values, not a string")`
findings.explanation: The exception is ValueError, raised from __post_init__ on IsIn, NotIn, Intersects and NotIntersects. Runtime probe: C.IsIn('abc') raised ValueError. Code catching TypeError would miss it.

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when float(old) < threshold <= float(new) .
findings.explanation: The boundary is inverted. The code fires when old is at or below the threshold and new is strictly above it. Runtime probe with threshold 25: CrossedAbove(25)(25, 26) returned True and CrossedAbove(25)(24, 25) returned False; the documented formula gives the reverse for both.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when float(old) <= threshold < float(new).

findings.doc_quote: Excludes last_reported , last_updated , and last_changed by default.
findings.explanation: The default exclusion list also contains context, which the page omits.
findings.suggested_fix: Excludes last_reported, last_updated, last_changed, and context by default.

summary: Most of the page is accurate: the accessor tables, literal coercion rules, Comparison operators and nearly all signatures match the code. There are 8 findings, 7 of them high severity, and they cluster in behavior details of individual rows: AttrDidChange with no old state, Contains case sensitivity, the CrossedAbove boundary, the collection exception type and the Guard field name. The other recurring error is the claim, on lines 9 and 28, that ChangeType and ValueIs conditions accept glob strings, when bare strings are compared exactly outside ServiceDataWhere and the *Matches predicates. claims_checked is an approximate count of the claims reviewed.
